100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 11, 1926, the United States faced a growing wave of labor strikes, with coal miners in Pennsylvania and textile workers in New England demanding better wages and working conditions. In Europe, the British government announced plans to address ongoing tensions in Ireland, as negotiations continued over the future of the Irish Free State. Meanwhile, in the realm of entertainment, the film industry buzzed with excitement over the upcoming release of "The Great Gatsby," set to captivate audiences with its lavish portrayal of the Roaring Twenties.
